speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you have noticed any fever, chills, or redness spreading around the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The patient's history of Crohn's disease, recent corticosteroid use for uveitis, and the painful, expanding ulcerative lesion following a minor trauma (ant bite) are classic presentations for this neutrophilic dermatosis, which requires a biopsy to rule out infection and malignancy before initiating systemic immunosuppression.
